label: finboost-p1-diag
_why: PROBE 1 OF AT MOST FIVE for the finish boost (user-ruled 2026-09-23: 'when there are enough points to finish the tech instantly, the AI has a very high priority for that'; 5-year probes pre-authorised, no more than five). ARM: {kind: config} on config/mod_config.probe-fin-diag.json = the canon (canon-slide-b158) with research_events.industry_bar_months 24 -> 6 so journal-entry stages actually complete inside five years, and research_events.finish_boost {enabled: FALSE, diag: TRUE}. The boost is OFF: this is the BASELINE of how the AI treats a paid-for technology, and the measurement of the engine's own tech cost. Not a candidate book.

_questions.Q1_penalty_formula: Does the engine's own cost (GetTechnology(X).GetCost(country)) equal era_cost x (1 + 0.25 x Σ), Σ = Σ(era − their era) over unresearched same-category techs of earlier eras? Read from PMR_AOT lines (every unresearched era-2+ tech, every country, windows 1836.2 and 1840.1) and PMR_FINC lines.
_questions.Q2_sericulture: Which reading matches: sa (sericulture COUNTED for the ~99% who never hold it) or sr (skipped)? They differ by exactly (era − 1) on every production tech of a non-holder, so one window decides it. The shipping value of finish_boost.unresearchable is set from this.
_questions.Q3_has_technology_progress: The registered-but-never-used trigger: h50 / h100 flags against prog / cost from PMR_FINC. Fraction-of-cost semantics predicts h100 = 1 exactly when prog >= cost.
_questions.Q4_baseline_pick: Without the boost, how long does a finishable technology (engine truth: prog >= cost) wait before the AI researches it, and what share of PMR_PICK choices land on one when one is available (nel > 0)?

_predictions.Q1: At least 95% of PMR_AOT lines match era_cost x (1 + 0.25 x Σ) exactly under ONE of the two readings. Mismatches, if any, come from the power-bloc principle that lowers the penalty (none should exist by 1840).
_predictions.Q2: NO confident prior — roughly a coin flip, which is why it is measured rather than argued. If the engine counts sericulture, the tooltip of every Western production tech above era 1 would list it, and nobody seems to have complained; if it skips it, the engine must special-case can_research = no.
_predictions.Q3: Fraction-of-cost semantics (h100 == [prog >= cost], h50 == [prog >= cost/2]) in at least 95% of lines.
_predictions.Q4: Finishable technologies wait: median latency from first finishable pulse to acquisition above 6 months, and fewer than half of the picks made while nel > 0 go to a finishable one.

_cost: 1 run x 1836.1.1 -> 1841.1.1, about 6-8 minutes of game time plus the build.
_watch: ~5 min: the PM_TECH_REHAUL marker, the version line, the error window BY POSITION, the clock, and PMR_ lines appearing in logs_live/debug.log
error.log: any line naming zzz_pm_rehaul_finish_diag or zzz_pm_rehaul_finish_values — a data function or trigger the engine rejects (has_technology_progress's comparator form is the untrodden one)
_caveats: industry_bar_months 6 is a PROBE setting that makes research far faster than the canon's; nothing here measures the canon's research pace.
No stop watcher: a five-year probe carries no register reading.
Launch ONLY through tools/testbed/launch_detached.ps1 CALLED DIRECTLY from the PowerShell tool (landmine L30).
